citation: Schochet, P., Cook, T., Deke, J., Imbens, G., Lockwood, J.R., Porter, J., Smith, J. (2010). Standards for Regression Discontinuity Designs. Retrieved from What Works Clearinghouse website: http://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/pdf/wwc_rd.pdf.
title: Establish the integrity of the forcing variable both institutionally and statistically before trusting RD impact estimates
description: Standard 1 requires that no systematic manipulation of the forcing variable occurred, since manipulation makes "the true relationship between the outcome and forcing variable can no longer be identified, which could lead to biased impact estimates." Institutional integrity requires describing who scored, who chose the cutoff, and when; statistical integrity requires a density test or graphical analysis around the cutoff. Both criteria must be satisfied to meet the standard without reservations.
requirements: An adequate description of the scoring and treatment assignment process showing scorers had little opportunity or incentive to change true scores
A statistical test failing to reject continuity of the forcing variable density at the cutoff, or a graphical density analysis without strong evidence of a discontinuity at the cutoff
constraints: If there is both a clear opportunity to manipulate scores and a clear incentive, the study does not satisfy this standard
target_learning_goals: credible causal estimates of education intervention effects
examples: Manipulation is likely to be less plausible if the forcing variable is a standardized test score than if it is a teacher-conducted assessment where teachers also influence treatment assignment.
key_sources: Schochet, P., Cook, T., Deke, J., Imbens, G., Lockwood, J.R., Porter, J., Smith, J. (2010). Standards for Regression Discontinuity Designs. Retrieved from What Works Clearinghouse website: http://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/pdf/wwc_rd.pdf.

citation: Schochet, P., Cook, T., Deke, J., Imbens, G., Lockwood, J.R., Porter, J., Smith, J. (2010). Standards for Regression Discontinuity Designs. Retrieved from What Works Clearinghouse website: http://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/pdf/wwc_rd.pdf.
title: RD studies must meet RCT attrition standards, reporting overall and differential attrition
description: Standard 2 requires RD studies to report the numbers assigned to treatment and comparison samples and response rates, with both overall attrition and attrition by treatment status. To meet the standard without reservations, "an RD study must meet the WWC randomized control trial (RCT) standards for attrition," calculated for the entire sample or only for units near the cutoff. A study failing this standard may still be reviewed as a QED if baseline equivalence is established.
requirements: Report overall attrition and attrition by treatment status
constraints: A study that fails this standard could potentially be reviewed as a QED if equivalence is established on key baseline covariates, with the forcing variable not exempt from the equivalence requirement
target_learning_goals: credible causal estimates of education intervention effects
examples: Attrition may be calculated either for the entire research sample or for only students near the cutoff value of the forcing variable.
key_sources: Schochet, P., Cook, T., Deke, J., Imbens, G., Lockwood, J.R., Porter, J., Smith, J. (2010). Standards for Regression Discontinuity Designs. Retrieved from What Works Clearinghouse website: http://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/pdf/wwc_rd.pdf.

citation: Schochet, P., Cook, T., Deke, J., Imbens, G., Lockwood, J.R., Porter, J., Smith, J. (2010). Standards for Regression Discontinuity Designs. Retrieved from What Works Clearinghouse website: http://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/pdf/wwc_rd.pdf.
title: Demonstrate continuity of the outcome-forcing variable relationship at the cutoff via covariate equivalence and placebo tests away from the cutoff
description: Standard 3 addresses the untestable smoothness condition underlying RD estimates through two indirect approaches: testing whether key baseline covariates correlated with the outcome are continuous at the cutoff, and testing for discontinuities at values away from the cutoff "where there should be no impacts." Both criteria must be satisfied to meet the standard without reservations; the covariate requirement is waived for the forcing variable itself.
requirements: Baseline equivalence on key covariates demonstrated at the cutoff value (waived for the forcing variable)
No evidence of an unexplainable discontinuity in the outcome-score relationship at score values other than the cutoff
constraints: The smoothness condition cannot be checked directly; the two approaches are indirect
target_learning_goals: credible causal estimates of education intervention effects
examples: Discontinuities away from the cutoff are tested at values such as the medians of points above or below the cutoff, following Imbens and Lemieux (2008); a discontinuity corresponding to another known intervention with a different cutoff is explainable.
key_sources: Schochet, P., Cook, T., Deke, J., Imbens, G., Lockwood, J.R., Porter, J., Smith, J. (2010). Standards for Regression Discontinuity Designs. Retrieved from What Works Clearinghouse website: http://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/pdf/wwc_rd.pdf.

citation: Schochet, P., Cook, T., Deke, J., Imbens, G., Lockwood, J.R., Porter, J., Smith, J. (2010). Standards for Regression Discontinuity Designs. Retrieved from What Works Clearinghouse website: http://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/pdf/wwc_rd.pdf.
title: Estimate RD impacts with a statistical model controlling for the forcing variable, an appropriate functional form, and a justified bandwidth
description: Standard 4 sets five criteria for statistical modeling, which "plays a central role in estimating impacts in an RD study." It is "never acceptable to estimate an impact by comparing the mean outcomes of treatment and comparison group members without adjusting for the forcing variable." Studies must include a graphical analysis, justify the parametric or nonparametric specification, support any slope constraint, and estimate site impacts separately for multi-site averages.
requirements: A statistical model controlling for the forcing variable
A graphical analysis with scatter plot and fitted curve consistent with the chosen bandwidth and functional form
Evidence that an appropriate parametric, semi-parametric, or nonparametric model was fit
Empirical support for any constraint that the relationship is the same on both sides of the cutoff
Separate site-level estimation when impacts are averaged across multiple sites
constraints: Meeting with reservations requires Criteria A and D plus either B or C; the study fails if Criterion A is not satisfied, or Criterion D is not satisfied, or both B and C are not satisfied
target_learning_goals: credible causal estimates of education intervention effects
examples: A polynomial degree could be chosen to minimize the Akaike Information Criteria, or a local regression bandwidth justified using cross-validation; sensitivity of impacts to tail observations can assess bandwidth choice.
key_sources: Schochet, P., Cook, T., Deke, J., Imbens, G., Lockwood, J.R., Porter, J., Smith, J. (2010). Standards for Regression Discontinuity Designs. Retrieved from What Works Clearinghouse website: http://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/pdf/wwc_rd.pdf.

article_title: Research and Development in America's Schools
citation: Smith, K. A., & Stewart, J. (2026, January). Research and development in America’s schools: How school systems drive sustainable improvement and innovation. Digital Promise. https://doi.org/10.51388/20.500.12265/283
title: R&D should be treated as a core function of healthy school systems, like budgeting, curriculum, and assessment
description: The report argues that school-system R&D is not optional but essential infrastructure. It states that "R&D must be considered a core function of healthy school systems, just like budgeting, curriculum, and assessment", positioning systematic inquiry and development alongside standard operational functions. The report frames this as what allows systems to become "engines of improvement and innovation" that design, implement, and scale solutions responsive to student needs.
requirements: System-level commitment to embedding inquiry, evidence, and collaboration into daily routines rather than isolated pilots
constraints: The report notes many systems engage in R&D without formal structures, and efforts "can be difficult to operationalize or scale" without a systematic structure
target_learners: K-12 students in school districts and charter networks
target_learning_goals: Improving teaching and learning outcomes through system-level improvement and innovation
examples: The report's framework, rubric, and three use cases (rural, suburban, charter network) are offered as ways to operationalize R&D as a core function
key_sources: Smith, K. A., & Stewart, J. (2026, January). Research and development in America’s schools: How school systems drive sustainable improvement and innovation. Digital Promise. https://doi.org/10.51388/20.500.12265/283

article_title: Teaching Responsible Data Science: Charting New Pedagogical Territory
citation: Lewis Armanda; Stoyanovich Julia. (2021). Teaching Responsible Data Science: Charting New Pedagogical Territory. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-021-00241-7
title: Teach ethics and responsibility early in the data science program and keep prerequisites minimal to enroll a diverse student group
description: The RDS course requires only an introductory data science or computer science course, deliberately excluding machine learning as a prerequisite. "This is a deliberate choice that reflects our goals to (1) educate data science students on ethics and responsibility early in their program of study, and (2) to enroll a diverse group of students." The semester-long course is structured as six thematic modules combining case studies, algorithmic and statistical insights, and hands-on exercises with open-source datasets and software libraries.
requirements: Students are expected to have basic familiarity with the python programming language, which is used in labs and assignments.
constraints: The authors faced a lack of a textbook offering comprehensive coverage of RDS balancing case studies, social-science concepts, and statistical and algorithmic techniques, so the course has no required textbook.
target_learners: graduate and advanced undergraduate data science students, including first-year students
target_learning_goals: ethics and responsibility in data science
algorithmic fairness, privacy, transparency, and interpretability
examples: The six modules span introduction, the data science lifecycle with profiling and cleaning, algorithmic fairness and diversity, privacy and data protection, transparency and interpretability, and ethical, legal, and regulatory frameworks.
Students are encouraged to attend public hearings of the New York City Committee on Technology on regulation of Automated Decision Systems and reflect on them in discussion.
key_sources: Lewis Armanda; Stoyanovich Julia. (2021). Teaching Responsible Data Science: Charting New Pedagogical Territory. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-021-00241-7

article_title: RDU Model dedicated to evaluate needed counsels for Serious Game projects
citation: Julian Alvarez, Jean-Yves Plantec, Mathieu Vermeulen, Christophe Kolski. (2017). RDU Model dedicated to evaluate needed counsels for Serious Game projects. Computers and Education. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2017.06.007
title: RDU model classifies counsels for Serious Game projects into Realization, Dissemination and Use
description: The RDU model is a classification framework for the counsels (accompaniments) needed across the lifecycle of Serious Game projects. The article states: "We propose to classify all these counsels in three main categories: R for Realization, D for Dissemination, and U for Use. By this way, we obtain a model named RDU." Its purpose is to support ownership adoption and appropriate use of a Serious Game within a dedicated ecosystem such as a school or hospital.
requirements: Projects need counsels addressed to Realization, Dissemination and Use in order to achieve adoption and intended use
constraints: The model addresses Serious Game projects deployed in dedicated ecosystems such as schools or hospitals
target_learners: learners using Serious Games in dedicated ecosystems such as schools and hospitals
target_learning_goals: appropriate use of Serious Games as intended by their designers
key_sources: Julian Alvarez, Jean-Yves Plantec, Mathieu Vermeulen, Christophe Kolski. (2017). RDU Model dedicated to evaluate needed counsels for Serious Game projects. Computers and Education. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2017.06.007

article_title: A pilot study of digital technology combined with case-based learning in clinical implantology training for specialists.
citation: Cai Z, Liu Y. (2025). A pilot study of digital technology combined with case-based learning in clinical implantology training for specialists. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08176-6
title: Ray Medical RD-100 oral surgery robot and implant navigation platform used as the digital teaching infrastructure
description: The digital infrastructure of the training program is Ray Medical's oral robot RD-100, described as the first oral surgery robot product certified by NMPA in China, comprising a Universal Robots manipulator, a Claron Technology optical tracking and positioning device, a North China Industrial Control mainframe, and RemeDent surgical navigation software. The article reports that "With the precise positioning assistance of the robot, doctors can accurately complete the surgery, and the precision error is controlled within 1° and 0.5 mm." Patient imaging came from original Dicom-format CBCT data, and model scanning used a Carestream CS 3600. The platform was already installed in the outpatient department and Clinical Skills Center, supports data reuse and remote instruction, and the pilot incurred no additional material or consumable costs.
requirements: Existing clinical datasets in Dicom CBCT format, a model scanner (Carestream CS 3600), and an installed navigation platform with workstations for independent trainee practice
constraints: The article states digital equipment is relatively expensive and the number of units in the department is limited, requiring appointment scheduling when many students practice
target_learners: oral and maxillofacial surgery specialists in implantology training
target_learning_goals: implant plan design and surgical simulation
examples: The imaging data of the typical case was stored in the implant navigation system, and after design was completed on the digital platform, the operation was performed with the assistance of the navigation system
key_sources: Cai Z, Liu Y. (2025). A pilot study of digital technology combined with case-based learning in clinical implantology training for specialists. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-08176-6
